name: 2025-2026_Objectives_For_Gasses
body:
2020-2021 Gas and Kinetic Molecular Theory (KMT)
Essential Questions (EQ4): Do and/or how do basic particles interact - Stay same? Each student will be able to:
1. Explain the kinetic molecular theory (i.e. ideal gas condition) with respect to gas phase and what the major gas parameters mean (T, P, V, and n). (Hint: Gas behavior video)
2. Using the kinetic molecular theory, explain the relationship (including doing calculations) between:
*Pressure (P) and volume (V) (Boyle's law) *Pressure (P) and (T) temperature (No-Name i.e. Gay-Lussac's Law ) *Volume (V) and (T) temperature (Charles' law) *Number of particles (n) and volume (V) of in a gas sample (Avogadro's hypothesis).
3. Explain the relationship between temperature and average kinetic energy.
4. Perform calculations using the ideal gas law including the gas constant, R.
As part of this, understand the molar volume (i.e. volume of a mole of gas) is a constant for any gas at a specific temperature and pressure. Specifically for 273K and 1.0 atm (that is what STP stands for Standard Temperature and Pressure)), the molar volume is 22.4L per 1.0 mole.

body:
Rate of Reaction - Clock Lab
Chemical Reactions



Part I : Effect of concentration on rate of reaction:
Directions(Procedures)

1. Add the appropriate amount of Solution A (see table below for volumes) and amount of water to the 100ml beaker.

2. Pour out the appropriate amount of Solution B into 25ml graduated cylinder.DO NOT ADD TO 100ml BEAKER UNTIL HAVE STOPWATCH

3. Add all Solution B into 100ml beaker at once, START STOPWATCH and swirl solutions until "solution turns blue". RECORD TIME

4. Dispose of solution into sink and clean 100ml beaker. Use only one graduate cylinder for each solution for all trials

Part II : Effect of Temperature on rate of reaction:
Directions(Procedures)

1. Make a 250mL or 400mL beaker of cold water using ice (below ambient temp) and another beaker with "hot water" (above ambient temp).

2. Add the 10ml of Solution A into a large test tube and then another 10mL of Solution A into a different large test tube.

3. Do the same for Solution B. Make a mark with wax pencil on either test to be able to tell which test tube has which solution.

4. Keep test tubes in cold water bath (should have 2 test tube, one A and one B) and same in hot water bath. Wait about 4 minutes, record temperature with a thermometer for hot water bath.

5. At exactly same time, add Solution A and Solution B into your 100mL reaction beaker and START TIMER. Swirl to mix as you place 100mL beaker into Hot water bath (have to take test tubes out).

6. STOP TIMER when you "see" color change. Record time in you data table along with temperature.

7. Dispose of solution in 100mL reaction beaker and wash/dry out.

8. Repeat Steps 4 thru 7 for cold water bath (FYI, you could do these steps in reverse, cold then hot)
